title: Dawn at the Observatory — The Last Command
translationStatus: Confession-reversal Japanese is authored in docs/36. Every other Japanese line is a draft machine-assisted translation awaiting native review.

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Regal contempt from above; unhurried, enjoying the echo.
lines.en: You have cracked my Bell and mistaken damage for mortality. Dawn is an old clerk; it has declared me dead before.
lines.ja: 我が鐘を砕き、傷を死と取り違えたか。夜明けなど老いた書記にすぎぬ。余の死を告げたのは、これが初めてではない。

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Persuasive, almost kind; each clause a ledger entry. Twist the knife on 'You counted them for me.'
lines.en: I made appetite predictable. A tax instead of a raid. A registry instead of a pogrom. Fewer graves, Father. You counted them for me.
lines.ja: 余は飢えを読めるものにした。略奪ではなく年貢を。虐殺ではなく戸籍を。墓は減ったのだ、神父。数えたのは、お前だろう。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Low, exhausted, precise. Guilt held under the voice, not performed.
lines.en: I counted fewer graves because you taught me not to count the people still breathing inside them.
lines.ja: 墓が減ったのは、その中でまだ息をしている者を数えるなと、お前に教えられたからだ。

lines.speaker: nikola
lines.direction: Magnificent, overconfident proclamation; he is enjoying himself far too much.
lines.en: This iron opened the side of Christ. I shall now prove Christianity superior by using the same spear to kill you.
lines.ja: この鉄は、キリストの脇腹を開いたものだ。同じ槍で貴様を討ち、我が信仰の優越を証明してみせよう。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Bone-dry correction; a tired scholar who cannot let an error stand even now.
lines.en: It did not kill Christ. He was already dead. Your threat is theologically and anatomically inaccurate.
lines.ja: それでキリストが死んだのではない。すでに息絶えておられた。お前の脅しは、神学的にも解剖学的にも不正確だ。

lines.speaker: nikola
lines.direction: Undaunted, breezy.
lines.en: You may correct the inscription after I use it.
lines.ja: 碑文の訂正は、使い終えてから頼む。

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Rising scorn; a prosecutor turning the court against the accusers.
lines.en: Listen to yourselves. One foreign faith names its violence love. One frontier covenant names its fear duty. You crossed the world to condemn my peace.
lines.ja: 己の言葉を聞くがいい。異国の信仰は己の暴力を愛と呼び、辺境の盟約は己の恐怖を義務と呼ぶ。そうして海を越え、余の泰平を裁きに来たか。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: The thesis of the game. Quiet, absolute, every word placed like a stone.
lines.en: We called our violence love. You called yours peace. The dead were not confused by either word.
lines.ja: 我々は己の暴力を愛と呼んだ。お前は己のそれを泰平と呼んだ。死者は、どちらの言葉にも惑わされなかった。

lines.speaker: miyo
lines.direction: Steady anger from someone used as an argument; she refuses both men.
lines.en: My mother kept me alive. The Senda house kept me alive. You do not get to use my pulse as a receipt for either of you.
lines.ja: 私を生かしたのは母です。センダの家です。私の脈を、あなたたちどちらの領収書にもさせません。

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Intimate, seductive, almost fatherly; a voice offering a warm room.
lines.en: Avelar, come home. I never asked you to become good, only useful.
lines.ja: アヴェラール、帰ってこい。善くなれと言ったことはない。役に立てと言っただけだ。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Refusal without heat; the pain of seeing the trap clearly at last.
lines.en: You asked me to become empty enough that usefulness felt like shelter.
lines.ja: お前が求めたのは、役に立つことが隠れ家に思えるほど、私が空っぽになることだった。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Invocation; full voice, the rite opening outward.
lines.en: Black Sun Concord!
lines.ja: 黒陽の盟約！

lines.speaker: nikola
lines.direction: Mid-lunge quip.
lines.en: Try not to make it sound like a committee.
lines.ja: 委員会のように言うな。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Clipped, under exertion.
lines.en: Try not to miss.
lines.ja: 外すなよ。

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Pinned under the spear, breathing hard, still bargaining from the floor. The trap, stated plainly.
lines.en: Kill me and every ambitious governor inherits an emergency. Keep me and you inherit my necessity.
lines.ja: 余を殺せば、野心ある代官どもが非常の世を受け継ぐ。生かせば、余という必要を受け継ぐのだ。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Measured verdict; the smallest humiliation delivered with great care.
lines.en: You wanted history to need you forever. Dawn offers the smaller humiliation: history continuing while you watch.
lines.ja: お前は、歴史に永遠に必要とされたかった。夜明けが与えるのは、もっと小さな屈辱だ。お前の目の前で、歴史が続いていくという屈辱だ。

lines.speaker: ren
lines.direction: Young, firm, no grandstanding. The last word before the choice.
lines.en: No. The weapon defeated you. Conversation decides whether defeat becomes anything except another grave.
lines.ja: 違う。お前を倒したのは武器だ。その敗北が、ただの墓で終わるかどうか。それを決めるのは、言葉だ。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Two centuries of restraint break at once. Raw, shouted, voice cracking.
lines.en: You killed my son!
lines.ja: お前は私の息子を殺した！

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Shouting back, defensive, the sovereign mask slipping.
lines.en: There was no other way, Mateus! He was a rebel!
lines.ja: ほかに道はなかった、マテウス！　あれは謀反人だった！

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Sudden quiet after the shout; almost a whisper, unbearable.
lines.en: You made me watch his execution.
lines.ja: お前は私に、あの子の処刑を見届けさせた。

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Lashing out; cruelty as self-defense.
lines.en: You demanded the right!
lines.ja: 見届ける権利を求めたのは、お前だ！

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Thunderous accusation; the heart of the game.
lines.en: Do not speak to me of burden. You made me betray my God!
lines.ja: “重荷”を語るな。お前は私に、神を裏切らせた！

lines.speaker: nikola
lines.direction: Ecclesiastical Latin (Italianate vowels), low and grave; for once no performance at all.
lines.en: Credis in Deum, Shogun?
lines.ja: Credis in Deum, Shogun?

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Translating, steady, giving the question its full weight.
lines.en: Shogun. He asks whether you believe in God.
lines.ja: 将軍。神を信じるか、と聞いている。

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Mandatory plain answer. A frightened ordinary man, no sovereign voice, barely audible.
lines.en: ...Yes.
lines.ja: ……はい。

lines.speaker: mateus
lines.direction: Firm, almost gentle; the sentence of a confessor, not a victor.
lines.en: Then do not call it a price. Call it sin.
lines.ja: ならば、“代価”と言うな。“罪”と言え。

lines.speaker: kurozane
lines.direction: Begins with the imperial 'yo', catches himself, and finishes as 'watashi': the sovereign fiction ending mid-sentence.
lines.en: Not by my... not by my authority. By the authority of those who live after me.
lines.ja: 余の――……私の権威ではない。私の後を生きる者たちの権威によって。
